Coumba Kebe

Democratic candidate for Treasurer of State, Indiana · Challenger

Health care executive (health care operations and compliance)

Coumba Kebe is a health care executive from Noblesville who was born in Indianapolis and is a first-generation American. She ran in the 2026 Democratic primary for Indiana House District 29 and lost to Devon Wellington. Delegates at the Indiana Democratic Party convention on June 6, 2026, then nominated her for State Treasurer, and she faces Republican incumbent Daniel Elliott on November 3, 2026.

Where Kebe stands

Transparency of state finances
Supports making financial reports easier to find and understand. Says the office should explain them through social media, press conferences and plain language, and that transparency means more than posting the information.
State investments (Israeli state bonds)
Questions whether Indiana's investments in Israeli state bonds bring the best possible returns. Argues that investment decisions should put financial performance ahead of political considerations.
State reserves
Says Indiana should keep reserves, but questions celebrating billions in reserves while residents struggle to pay their bills.
Local government financing (Indiana Bond Bank)
Proposes assessing needs in all 92 counties and giving priority to low-interest loans for communities that need them, especially rural communities with infrastructure needs.
Disaster response
Says local governments need a faster response after disasters, and proposes that the treasurer's office focus on financial resources and assistance after a disaster.
Savings programs (CollegeChoice 529, ABLE)
Proposes raising public awareness of existing programs such as the CollegeChoice 529 education savings plan and ABLE accounts for eligible people with disabilities.
Role of the office
Says the office can explain the financial effects of lawmakers' decisions and advocate for solutions on child care and health care access, while acknowledging the treasurer does not set state policy.

Background

  • 2026: Democratic nominee for Indiana State Treasurer (state convention, June 6, 2026)
  • 2026: Candidate in the Democratic primary for Indiana House District 29; lost to Devon Wellington
  • About 10 years in health care operations, including roles as corporate compliance and training officer and director of field operations
  • Education: Indiana University, B.S. in Community Health and Preventive Medicine; Master of Public Health in Health Policy and Management
  • Graduate of Franklin Central High School; lives in Noblesville
